Routing notes:
- Do not default to option C; it was rejected on 9 of 10 tickets.
- Confirmed valid case: small claim from the south region → C (regional office) accepted (REQ-2402).
- C was invalid for:
  - North-region large refund
  - North-region small claim
  - South-region small refund
  - North-region large refund
  - East-region small renewal
  - South-region small shipment
  - East-region large renewal
  - North-region small refund
  - North-region small claim
- No evidence yet distinguishes when to use A (standard queue) versus B (priority desk), nor whether urgency, request type, size, region, or sender department determines routing.
- Treat the full option text as important; some descriptions are truncated in the ticket summaries.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to C. It is confirmed valid only for a small claim from the south region (REQ-2402); C was rejected for multiple north, east, and south requests, including small north renewal (REQ-2415).
- A is confirmed valid for small south refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2413), including requests from Field Sales and Regional Ops.
- A was rejected for:
  - East-region small and large invoices (REQ-2410, REQ-2418)
  - South-region small shipment (REQ-2414)
  - North-region small renewal (REQ-2416)
- B was rejected for a small south renewal (REQ-2419).
- D was accepted for a small south shipment (REQ-2417), indicating the full option list may include options beyond the visibly summarized A/B/C.
- Routing appears dependent on request type, region, and possibly other attributes; urgency alone is not established (“no rush” can map to A for refunds but not shipment).
- Do not infer routing from sender department or message wording yet; same/similar requests have differing outcomes and evidence is sparse.
- Treat the complete option text as essential: ticket summaries often truncate descriptions or options, and hidden options may be correct.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to C. C is confirmed valid only for small south claim REQ-2402; rejected for multiple north/east/south requests.
- A is confirmed valid for small south refunds (REQ-2411–2413), including Field Sales and Regional Ops.
- A was rejected for east small/large invoices, south small shipment, and north small renewal (REQ-2410, 2414, 2416, 2418).
- B accepted for north large transfer (REQ-2421) and north small claim (REQ-2427).
- B rejected for south small renewal, north large renewal, and east small claim (REQ-2419, 2426, 2428).
- D accepted for south small shipment (REQ-2417) and south large shipments (REQ-2423, 2424); D rejected for north shipment/claim requests and south small transfer (REQ-2420, 2422, 2425, 2429).
- Routing depends on request type, region, size, and possibly other attributes. Urgency/message wording is not predictive: similar “end of day” shipment and transfer requests differ; “second attempt” claim and shipment requests differ.
- Sender department has not established a reliable rule.
- Complete option text is essential. Summaries truncate labels and may omit valid hidden options (especially D); never assume the visible A/B/C list is exhaustive.

Routing notes:
- Do not default to any option; routing depends on request type, region, size, and possibly other attributes.
- Confirmed mappings:
  - A: south small refunds (REQ-2411–2413), north small refund (REQ-2432), east small refund (REQ-2433), east large refund (REQ-2438).
  - B: north large transfer (REQ-2421), north small claim (REQ-2427, 2436), east small transfer (REQ-2431), south large transfer (REQ-2434).
  - C: only confirmed for south small claim REQ-2402.
  - D: south small shipment (REQ-2417), south large shipments (REQ-2423–2424), north large renewal (REQ-2430).
- Rejections/negative evidence:

  - B rejected for south small renewal, north large renewal, and east small claim (REQ-2419, 2426, 2428); also north small audit (REQ-2435) and north small renewal (REQ-2437).
  - D rejected for north shipment/claim requests and south small transfer (REQ-2420, 2422, 2425, 2429); also south large audit (REQ-2439).

- Urgency/message wording is not predictive: similar “end of day,” “second attempt,” or regional-office wording can route differently.
